title: [source-mongodb-v2] Failed syncs due to [config_error] Saved offset is not valid.
body:
### Connector Name

source-mongodb-v2

### Connector Version

2.0.1

### What step the error happened?

During the sync

### Relevant information

Hi, 
I'm having random issues failing syncs with error coming up : 
`[config_error] Saved offset is not valid. Please reset the connection, and then increase oplog retention and/or increase sync frequency to prevent his from happening in the future.`

I have to full refresh the connector to make it work again for a short time.
I have set sync to trigger every hour. It was set to every 3 hours before that and I encountered this issue.
I'm using Atlas MongoDB with an M30 cluster.

comments.author: whanata
comments.body:
[This issue came up after we upgraded the Mongo DB Source to `2`].

I have the same issue with sync from `Mongo DB` to `Snowflake`.
`Saved offset is not valid.`.

Airbyte OSS - `1.5.1`
Mongo DB Source - `2.0.1`
Snowflake DB Destination - `3.15.10`

It happens twice already, a week apart on the same time.
This corresponds to the Oplog Window of 7 days I added in my Mongo DB Cluster.

One thing I noticed is that in `Connection state`, the `shared state` had 2 state.
```
"shared_state": {
  "state": {
    "[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]": <resume_token>,
    "[<mongo_url>]": <resume_token>
  },
  "schema_enforced": false
},
```

The `[<mongo_url>]` seems to have a resume token that's up to date (based of my syncs every hour).
The `"[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]"` resume token is the same and does not update at all.

I checked what the resume token is by just creating my own Mongo Change Stream and see what the first event was for that Resume Token.

The fix I did for the last 2 weeks was update the resume token of `"[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]"` with the Mongo URL Resume token on the other state.

I didn't have this issue when my Mongo DB Source was on version `1`, but I seem to have encountered the issue ever since I've upgraded the Mongo DB Source to version `2` which allows multiple different schemas within one Mongo DB Cluster. I don't utilise multiple schemas within a Mongo DB Cluster, so I'm only using it as having only 1 schema.

I was wondering if anyone knew why the Resume Token for `"[\"prod\",{\"server_id\":\"prod\"}]"` does not update in the first place or what is that specific state for? I assume that's the state of what it is in Snowflake, but I'm not entirely sure.

comments.author: yardencarmeli
comments.body:
@Tanujshriyan 24hour oplog retention may be too short for your workload.
Within that window, you need at least one successful sync that reads changes and advances the LSN. If the LSN does not advance before the oplog recycles, you can lose the position and the following sync will fail.

That being said, this seems unrelated to the “two states” bug tracked here, and we’d like to keep this ticket focused on that issue. Please open a new ticket with the details you shared so we can investigate further. If you have a support package, I also recommend reaching out to our Support team.

As a quick remedy, make sure you run a sync at least once per day and that it reads data so the LSN advances before oplog retention is reached. Hope it's helpful!

comments.author: lepagea01
comments.body:
Hello all,

As tests in our **DEV** environment looked promising, we upgraded our **STG** and **PROD** environments to **version 2.0.4** of the connector. I'm afraid to report that results are not as hoped for. We keep on having sync failures due to the _possibly misleading_ error below:

`Saved offset is not valid. Please reset the connection, and then increase oplog retention and/or increase sync frequency to prevent his from happening in the future.`

Problem is, we perform hourly syncs with MongoDB databases having **oplog sized for about 7 days worth of transactions**, based on Oplog GB/Hour. Still investigating minimum number of hours to preserve oplog entries with MongoDB teams here but, so far, settings seem OK.

Some details and observations:

- Looking into Airbyte's logs, we no longer see clearly that syncs are failing because they were using obviously outdated resume tokens. So far, so good.
- As confirmed in a previous comment, we no longer see dual entries in Airbyte's saved states. So far, so good.
- It may be unrelated but, we cannot help but noticing that syncs that are so far always successful save a _sane_ saved state such as:

```json
"state": {
      "[\"mongodb_srv___some_url_\",{\"server_id\":\"mongodb_srv___some_url_\"}]": "{\"sec\":0,\"ord\":-1,\"resume_token\":\"8268CEC1FA000000042B0429296E1404\"}"
    }
```

- On the other hand, syncs that repeatedly fail save a _strange_ state such as:

```json
"state": {
      "[\"mongodb_srv___some_url_\",{\"server_id\":\"mongodb_srv___some_url_\"}]": "{\"sec\":1758374666,\"ord\":15,\"resume_token\":\"8268CEAB0A0000000F2B042C0100296E5A10047366FF157A054D4E8913D208D2A32047463C6F7065726174696F6E54797065003C7265706C6163650046646F63756D656E744B657900465A5F6964005A10032AFCEABFAAC8494D9110E5DB7E63EC34000004\"}"
    }
```

What we observed:

- When things work as expected, epoch is 0 and resume token is a _small_ hash in the saved state
- When things fail, epoch is somewhat more meaningful than 0 but resume token is a _larger_ hash in the saved state.

As all our connections to MongoDB sources are configured in exactly the same way, difficult to understand this inconsistent behaviour. Again, it may be unrelated. Not exactly sure how **Debezium** generates tokens. But these observations are constant.

Please, let me know if I can share more info. Thx.

Do you have any read preference tags? Did this only occur in your prod environment? My suggestion is to open a new ticket with all the details (oplog retention, read preference tags, or any other relevant configuration differences between test and prod). Please feel free to reopen if you have any further questions.
